items.answer: Salt is a giant ionic lattice of sodium and chloride ions, and NaCl gives only the ratio
choices: Salt is made of NaCl molecules, each one sodium atom joined to one chlorine atom

items.prompt: Which statement about table salt is correct?

items.answer: Sodium gives its outer electron to chlorine, forming a positive sodium ion and a negative chloride ion
choices: They share a pair of electrons equally between them
Chlorine gives an electron to sodium, forming a chloride ion
Sodium gives its outer electron to chlorine, forming a positive sodium ion and a negative chloride ion
Both atoms keep their electrons and are held by a sea of electrons
items.prompt: Sodium has electron arrangement 2,8,1 and chlorine has 2,8,7. What happens when they form sodium chloride?

items.answer: Each chlorine atom contributes one electron to a shared pair between the two atoms. Both atoms count the shared pair in their outer shell, so each has eight outer electrons. No electron is transferred, so no ions form.
items.prompt: A chlorine molecule, Cl2, is held together by a covalent bond. Explain, in terms of electrons, how the bond forms and why no ions are made.

items.answer: Copper is a lattice of positive metal ions in a sea of free-moving electrons. The electrons carry charge through the wire, so it conducts. The layers of ions can slide over each other while the sea still holds them, so the wire bends instead of shattering.
items.prompt: Explain, in terms of particles and electrons, why copper wire conducts electricity and can be bent without breaking.

items.answer: In the solid the ions are locked in the lattice; when molten they are free to move and carry charge
choices: Melting turns the lattice into NaCl molecules that carry the current
In the solid the ions are locked in the lattice; when molten they are free to move and carry charge
The solid contains no charged particles at all
Heat creates electrons inside the solid that carry the current
